ai.description: Tytler's Mabuya reaches 10 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a dark lateral stripe and pale dorsolateral lines. Distinctive features include a keeled mid-dorsal scale row and smooth limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis tytleri* is best distinguished by its distinctively long limbs and the presence of a single pair of nuchal scales, which are absent in similar Indian skinks.
ai.habitat: Tytler's Mabuya inhabits the tropical forests and coastal scrublands of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, typically found in leaf litter and near forest edges at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: Tytler's Mabuya is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky outcrops during the sunlit hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis tytleri* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Eutropis tytleri is endemic to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where it inhabits tropical forest environments across the archipelago.
